story: A sage asks another sage if a truly righteous man exists in the world, and learns of a prince named Rama. A king with three wives has no son; he performs a fire sacrifice, and the gods ask the god Vishnu to take mortal birth to destroy a demon king who terrorizes the universe. Four sons are born to the king's wives, the eldest being Rama. As a youth, Rama and his brother Lakshmana receive weapons from a sage and destroy demons. At a neighboring kingdom, Rama strings and breaks a legendary bow, winning the hand of princess Sita, who had been found in a field, and marries her. Before Rama can be crowned, his stepmother Kaikeyi, provoked by a servant, demands he be exiled fourteen years and her son Bharata be made king instead. The old king dies of grief. Sita and Lakshmana join Rama in exile. Bharata refuses the throne and rules only as regent. In the forest, a demoness tries to seduce the brothers and harm Sita; Lakshmana cuts off her nose and ears. Her brothers attack and are defeated. The demon king Ravana sends a rakshasa disguised as a golden deer to lure Rama away, then abducts Sita while Lakshmana is tricked into leaving her unguarded. A vulture tries to rescue her but is mortally wounded. Rama allies with monkey-people, kills their king's usurping brother to restore him to the throne, and gains the aid of the devoted Hanuman, who helps find Sita, held captive by Ravana, who wants to marry her but she refuses, remaining faithful. Rama ultimately wins the battle against Ravana and returns to his capital with Sita to be crowned king amid celebration.
